l0.MECHANISM: Protocol payment to external actors who initiate eligible vault liquidation or reset expired collateral auctions. Protocol health requires these state transitions. This is compensation for providing a service, not directional prediction after liquidations.
l0.WHO_PAYS: The documented Clipper incentives credit DAI to a keeper through Vow/Vat accounting; auction recovery and liquidation penalties support system accounting, but rewards are not demonstrated net revenue for a new participant. Distinguish this protocol-funded service payment from a bidder earning a collateral resale spread.
l0.WHY_PERSIST: The protocol needs timely independent calls and exposes configurable incentives to cover operating/risk costs. Gas, execution competition and operational capability can limit participation. Those frictions may absorb all payment; current persistent economic rent is not established.
l0.CHEAP_DATA_NOW: Public primary Sky documentation specifies Dog/Clipper, Bark/Redo transitions and governance-controlled incentive structure. Official Ethereum JSON-RPC documentation specifies address/topic/block filtering and reorg flags. No qualified no-account historical host or deployment/parameter mapping was established in this bounded scout.
l0.CHEAP_EXPRESSION: Potential future upper-bound falsification of externally funded Bark/Redo service rewards less all transaction costs under one frozen contract/time population. No event population, time window or economic rule declared; winner-only receipts could at most give a favorable upper bound, not a new entrant profitability estimate. Do not combine bidding spreads with service rewards.
l0.FATAL_PROBLEM: Rewards may be zero or ineligible; gas and unsuccessful competition can exceed rewards; winners are selected; front-running and composability allow imitation; active deployment/parameters may differ from conceptual docs; public schema is not usable free historical access. No L1 admissible now.
l0.WHY_NOT_ARBITRAGED: Not established. The same flash-collateral feature lowering capital requirements also lowers entry barriers and increases documented front-running exposure. Existing specialized keepers may compete away the gross incentive.
l0.causal_distinction: Service compensation by contract versus historical carry, post-liquidation signal, book-pressure or prediction-market arbitrage. Shared crypto/gas/liquidation exposure is retained; no independent-trial count asserted.

excerpts: The form of the incentive is, on a per-collateral type basis, a constant amount of DAI plus an amount of DAI that scales linearly with the amount of debt associated with the liquidation. Either contribution can be set to zero.
Clipper – tip: Flat fee to suck from vow to incentivize keepers when liquidating a vault or resetting an already existing auction.
Clipper – chip: Percentage of tab to suck from vow to incentivize keepers when liquidating a vault or resetting an already existing auction.
Flash Lending of Collateral: eliminates any capital requirement for bidders (excepting gas)
In liquidations 2.0 if a keeper chooses to participate with no capital, there is substantial front-running risk from generalized front-running bots.
There is one exception to this incentive. If the tab or lot * price remaining is under the Clipper.chost limit, then there will be no incentive paid to redo.
limitations: Illustrative numeric parameters and attack scenarios are documentation examples, not live values or observed profits.
Bark and Redo service rewards differ from a take bidder resale spread. They must not be mixed into one backtested return.

disconfirmation: Sky expressly permits either incentive component to be zero and excludes some redo rewards below chost.

Instant settlement/flash collateral mitigates inventory financing but makes the action easier to copy; no exclusive information advantage is evidenced.
Reorg flags and finalized filters help define records but do not prove RPC retention, free permission or contemporaneous transaction attainability.
